Hi Gay,

Many people who believe that the user interface has changed too much discover that they can easily make Thunderbird look the way that it did for them earlier. Sometimes an upgrade changes something that can be changed back. If you tell us what has changed, what you don't like, and what you prefer, we can probably help.

You may discover how to get Thunderbird to look the way you want by exploring some options under the "View" menu: View - Layou and View - Folders. If there is no menu across the top of your screen, press the <alt> key or click on ≡ at top right to show a menu there.

I wonder if an upgrade might switch between cards view and table view. If that is what is making reading your mail difficult, click on the film roll button at top right and pick the other view.

It is usually better to use more recent versions of Thunderbird because they are more secure.

content:
Many people both receive and send messages with large attachments, and the attachments will remain in your SENT and other folders. Although it takes some time and effort on your part, if you comb through your email folders you may find that there's no need to keep some attachments any more. Deleting them can significantly reduce the size of your message store.

If you view your Message List in Table Mode, you can add a Size column. You can then sort the list by size and easily see which messages are using the most room. See my attached image (I see I need to do some housecleaning myself!) After deleting any unneeded attachments, follow up by Compacting the folders.

Another thing that takes up a lot of room is the Global Search database ("global-messages-db.sqlite"). It tends to grow quite large but never shrink. For example, mine is currently 615 MB. The file can be deleted (while Thunderbird is closed) and will be regenerated when the program next runs. It can take up to a few hours to create a new database, and it might or might not be much smaller.

content:
Here's a thorough description of the various release channels:

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/choosing-thunderbird-release-channel

For most people, the choice is between the Release channel, which is the latest version, or the ESR channel, which is usually the next-to latest major release.

Despite the official recommendation, I personally recommend the ESR channel, unless you're willing to deal with rough edges and the possibility that your add-ons won't be compatible. I put off the Release version until it's more mature and time-tested, and when I've verified that my crucial add-ons are compatible.

content:
Gmail uses OAuth2 for authorization. In order for Thunderbird to complete the process, it needs to set a cookie. To make sure can can happen please do the following:

- Make sure cookies are allowed (<Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept cookies from sites>);

- Delete all cookies for that account (<Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Show Cookies>);

- Delete all passwords for that account from saved passwords (<Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | Saved Passwords>);

Now restart Thunderbird. You will be asked for your credentials, and hopefully they will be accepted and mail retrieval will resume.
